records.title: An annotated bibliography of hypobaric decompression sickness research conducted at the Crew Technology Division, USAF School of Aerospace Medicine, Brooks AFB, Texas from 1983 to 1988
records.note: 20 visually verified table rows. Study 8 is in progress and 120 is the planned exposure total. The table has two participant-level clinical percentage columns and provides no exposure-level percentage.

physical_units.onset: Grade 2 DCS mean in minutes among affected exposures, excluding delayed onset
physical_units.vge: Highest recorded grade on any exposure per participant
physical_units.oxygen: Oxygen percentage during exposure. The notes describe nitrogen balance for concentrations below 100%. The CO₂ prebreathe experiment has its own assigned gas mixtures.

reconciliation.finding: 18 rows match all comparable 1988 table cells. The revision adds exposure-level Grade 2 DCS percentages.
25,000-ft BSI revision reports 27 participants and 28 exposures versus 29 participants and 30 exposures in 1988. The numerator and reason for recategorization are not given.

CO₂ study three-hour stage has 77 exposures and 12% Grade 2 DCS. Six-hour stage has 49 exposures and 86%. Baas interim abstract gives 8/78. The 2010 archive describes 71 earlier and 50 longer exposures. Timepoints and case accounting remain distinct.

27,500-ft BSI row has 83 exposures and 73% Grade 2 DCS, with 144-minute conditional mean onset. The workshop gives 80% and 142 minutes on 83 exposures. NEDU compilation gives 66/83 at 27,600 ft. Olson gives 64/82 with a distinct clinical definition. The risk sets cannot be equated.
The 9.00-psia participant maximum VGE groups sum to 101% at printed precision. Values retained as published.

records.identifier: Space Life Sciences Symposium 1987 unpaginated addendum
records.note: The archived abstract heading is on printed p. 4 and the quantitative outcomes on p. 5. This Smead report is distinct from the preceding Krutz et al. 1986 abstract and reuses the parent BSI experiment.

observations.outcome_window: During chamber exposure scheduled for up to 8 hours. Grade 2 limb bends could trigger descent.
observations.note: The abstract gives 126 flights with limb bends and 64 without. Grade 2 was constant moderate pain that resolved on descent.

observations.note: Conditional on limb bends. The outcome requires bubbling before symptoms and cannot be used as an all-flight incidence rate.

observations.note: Conditional on absence of limb bends. Significant bubbling was Neuman grades 3–4. The two conditional summaries use different event definitions.

records.title: Effect of a carbon dioxide prebreathe gas mixture on the incidence of altitude-induced decompression sickness
records.note: Same interim abstract as the in-press reprint in ADA201274, printed pp. 13–14. This 78-flight snapshot is an earlier analysis from the Study 8 / VAX 23 program. Arm denominators are unavailable.

observations.outcome_window: At altitude through persistent symptoms or scheduled 3-hour end. Delayed surveillance is unavailable.
observations.note: Four cases in each arm. Per-arm denominators are unstated. The revision gives 77 exposures for the three-hour stage, with no exposure crosswalk.
